result: V1 interneuron clades exhibit distinct temporal patterns of neurogenesis. EdU birthdating experiments reveal that Renshaw cells and Pou6f2-V1s are early born (peak at E10.5 and E11.0 respectively), while Foxp2-V1s and Sp8-V1s are late born (peak at E11.5 and E12 respectively). Peak V1 neurogenesis occurs at E11 with 23.4%±2.9 of V1s incorporating EdU, and EdU labeling accounts for 49.8-68.2% of cells across different clades.
evaluation: Claims C15-C41 provide comprehensive EdU birthdating data across multiple embryonic timepoints (E9.5-E12.5) in multiple animals (n=3-6 per timepoint). The data consistently show distinct neurogenesis peaks for different V1 clades with appropriate statistical representation (mean±SD reported). The temporal resolution is adequate despite acknowledged limitations of 12hr injection intervals, and the stringent EdU labeling criteria strengthen the findings.

result: V1 interneuron clades born at different embryonic times settle in distinct spatial locations within the spinal cord. Early born MafB-V1s (E10) accumulate ventrally in the Renshaw cell area, while later born MafB-V1s (E10.5-E11) are Pou6f2-V1s occupying dorsal positions. Foxp2-V1 generation spans the entire neurogenesis period with location varying by birthdate in a clockwise rotation pattern, and Sp8-V1s show ventral-to-dorsal progression with later birthdates.
evaluation: Claims C42-C52 are supported by spatial mapping analyses combining EdU birthdating with cell position plotting (Figure 2). The data show clear spatial segregation patterns for different V1 clades and birthdates. The use of density contour plots and multiple animals per timepoint provides robust evidence for the spatial-temporal relationships described.

result: V1 clade marker expression differs between P0 and P5, with MafB showing the largest change (9.4%±1.6 at P5 vs 25% at P0). MafB is expressed at P0 in three V1 clades but is quickly downregulated after birth in Foxp2-V1s while maintained in Pou6f2-V1s and ventral Renshaw cells. When considering only ventral MafB-V1s in the Renshaw area, percentages are identical at P5 and P0 (5.5%±1.7 vs 5.0%).
evaluation: Claims C53-C60 are supported by quantitative immunocytochemistry data at P5 (n=19-26 mice depending on marker) compared to published P0 data. The large discrepancy in total MafB-V1 percentages is explained by developmental downregulation in specific clades, and this is validated by the identical percentages when restricting analysis to ventral Renshaw cells. The use of genetic labeling (MafB-GFP mice) provides additional validation.

result: Genetic lineage labeling reveals that Foxp2-V1 interneurons represent 59-66% of all V1s, approximately twice the number identified by postnatal Foxp2 protein expression (~32%). The proportions of Foxp2-V1s and non-Foxp2 V1s remain constant across postnatal ages (P0, P5, P15, adult) and spinal segments (Th13-S1). Only about half of genetically labeled Foxp2-V1 cells express Foxp2 protein at P5, and lineage-labeled Foxp2-V1s comprise 55.7%±4.7 of all spinal Foxp2+ neurons.
evaluation: Claims C62-C68 are supported by intersectional genetic labeling using En1cre and Foxp2flpo with dual reporters (n=2-6 mice across different ages and segments). The discrepancy between genetic lineage and protein expression is well-documented with appropriate controls showing lineage-labeled cells do not express other V1 clade markers. The consistency across ages and segments strengthens the conclusion that this represents a stable population with developmental Foxp2 downregulation.

result: Foxp2-V1 interneuron numbers significantly increase in limb-innervating segments (L3-L6) compared to axial/hypaxial segments (Th13, L1, S1) (p<0.0001, one-way ANOVA). The ratio of Foxp2-V1 interneurons to motoneurons remains relatively constant from Th13 to L5, suggesting parallel scaling with motoneuron numbers.
evaluation: Claims C69-C70 are supported by systematic quantification across spinal segments in P20 mice (n=3-5 mice, 4 ventral horns per segment). Statistical analysis is appropriate (one-way ANOVA with post hoc Bonferroni tests) and the parallel increase in Foxp2-V1s and motoneurons in limb segments is well-documented with density plots. The constant ratio provides strong evidence for coordinated scaling.

result: V1 synaptic targeting of motoneurons varies by motor column and V1 clade. HMC and lower lumbar LMC motoneurons receive significantly more V1 synapses than MMC motoneurons, with Foxp2-V1 axons providing higher synaptic densities than non-Foxp2-V1 axons in HMC and LMC (except L1/2). Renshaw cell synapses occur at lower densities than Foxp2-V1s in most LMC groups. Most synapses on HMC, LMC, and MMC motoneuron cell bodies originate from either Foxp2-V1s or Renshaw cells, while PGC neurons receive very low V1 input.
evaluation: Claims C71-C79 are supported by rigorous 3D reconstruction and quantification of synapses on motoneuron cell bodies (n=21-30 motoneurons per motor column from 5 animals). The methodology is well-described with stringent criteria for synapse identification (VGAT+ contacts on genetically labeled axons). Statistical analyses are appropriate (nested ANOVA, two-way ANOVA with Bonferroni corrections) and account for inter-animal variability. The convergent evidence from multiple genetic models strengthens the conclusions.

result: Foxp2-V1 interneurons exhibit molecular heterogeneity at P5. Approximately 50% express Otp and 20% express Foxp4, with Foxp4+ cells always co-localizing with Otp. A large group (44%) co-expressing Otp and Foxp2 is localized close to the LMC, including a smaller ventral subgroup (23%) also expressing Foxp4.
evaluation: Claims C80-C84 are supported by systematic immunolabeling combined with genetic lineage tracing in P5 mice (n=2-3 mice, multiple ventral horns analyzed). The co-localization analyses are quantitative and include spatial mapping showing distinct locations for different molecular subgroups. The hierarchical relationship (Foxp4+ cells are subset of Otp+ cells) is clearly demonstrated.

result: VGLUT1 synapses (proprioceptive inputs) preferentially target Foxp2-V1 interneurons expressing Otp and Foxp2 at P5. Overall, 63-74% of Foxp2-V1 interneurons receive VGLUT1 synapses, with 65.8% of VGLUT1-contacted cells expressing Otp and 82% of Otp+ Foxp2-V1s receiving VGLUT1 contacts. Among VGLUT1-contacted Foxp2-V1s, 85.6% of Otp+ cells also maintain Foxp2 expression and 89.8% of Foxp2+ cells are Otp+.
evaluation: Claims C85-C91 are supported by high-resolution confocal analysis of VGLUT1 synapses on genetically labeled Foxp2-V1 cells at P5 (n=2 mice, 12 ventral horns, 1116 cells analyzed). The methodology includes rigorous criteria for synapse identification and distinguishes proximal vs distal contacts. The convergent data from multiple marker combinations (Otp, Foxp2, VGLUT1) provides strong evidence for preferential proprioceptive targeting of specific Foxp2-V1 subgroups.

result: Combined anterograde tracing of tibialis anterior (TA) muscle sensory afferents and retrograde monosynaptic tracing from lateral gastrocnemius (LG) motoneurons confirms that Foxp2-V1 interneurons are positioned in reciprocal inhibitory pathways between antagonistic ankle muscles.
evaluation: Claim C24 is supported by proof-of-principle experiments using combined CTB anterograde labeling and rabies virus retrograde tracing (n=5 mice injected, 3 with successful transsynaptic labeling). While the data demonstrate that some Foxp2-V1 interneurons receive TA sensory input and project to LG motoneurons, the authors acknowledge significant technical limitations including low yield, age-dependent efficiency issues, and limited sampling. The variable number of TA synapses (5-31) on different Foxp2-V1 cells and the small sample size (8 Foxp2-V1 IaINs identified) limit the strength of conclusions. Additional experiments with higher yield techniques are needed for comprehensive validation.

result: Early born Renshaw cells and late born Foxp2-V1 interneurons are tightly coupled to motoneurons, while early born Pou6f2-V1 and late born Sp8-V1 interneurons are not. This indicates that timing of neurogenesis does not correlate with motoneuron targeting. The Foxp2-V1 clade provides the largest inhibitory input to motoneuron cell bodies.
evaluation: Claims C16-C18, C20 integrate birthdating data (Figure 1) with synaptic connectivity data (Figure 5) to demonstrate that both early-born (Renshaw) and late-born (Foxp2-V1) clades can be tightly coupled to motoneurons. The conclusion that birthdate doesn't predict motoneuron targeting is well-supported by the contrasting connectivity patterns of clades with similar birthdates. The quantitative synaptic density data clearly shows Foxp2-V1s provide the highest density input to motoneuron cell bodies, particularly in limb-related motor columns.

result: The Foxp2-V1 clade contains over half of all V1 interneurons and includes subgroups that differ in birthdate, location, and proprioceptive input.
evaluation: Claims C19 and C21 are supported by convergent evidence from genetic lineage labeling (59-66% of V1s, Figure 3), birthdating analyses showing temporal heterogeneity (Figure 1-2), spatial mapping showing location differences (Figures 2, 6), and VGLUT1 synapse analyses showing differential proprioceptive input (Figure 7). The integration of multiple experimental approaches provides strong support for Foxp2-V1 heterogeneity.

result: One Foxp2-V1 subgroup defined by postnatal Otp expression is positioned near the LMC, receives substantial proprioceptive input, and is consistent with involvement in reciprocal inhibitory pathways.
evaluation: Claims C22-C23 are supported by the combination of Otp expression analysis (Figure 6), spatial localization near LMC (Figure 6), VGLUT1 synapse analysis showing 82% of Otp+ Foxp2-V1s receive proprioceptive input (Figure 7), and circuit tracing experiments (Figure 8). While the circuit tracing has limitations (acknowledged in C24 evaluation), the convergent anatomical and connectivity data provide strong support for the proposed role in reciprocal inhibition. The location and input patterns match known characteristics of reciprocal Ia inhibitory interneurons.

result: Birthdate order is not predictive of presynaptic coupling to motoneurons or phylogenetic relations in V1 interneurons.
evaluation: Claim C92 is an inference well-supported by the data showing that both early-born (Renshaw cells) and late-born (Foxp2-V1s) clades are tightly coupled to motoneurons, while other early-born (Pou6f2-V1) and late-born (Sp8-V1) clades are not. This demonstrates that birthdate alone does not predict functional connectivity. The phylogenetic argument is supported by discussion of reciprocal and recurrent inhibition appearing at different evolutionary timepoints.

result: Background claims establish that V1 interneurons originate from p1 progenitors expressing En1, send ipsilateral projections throughout the ventral horn, densely innervate motoneurons, and play crucial roles in motor control. Prior work organized V1s into at least four major clades (Renshaw, Pou6f2, Foxp2, Sp8) based on P0 molecular identity, with V1 neurogenesis previously divided into early and late phases.
evaluation: Claims C1-C14 are background claims supported by appropriate citations to prior literature. These establish the foundation for the current study and are not primary findings of this manuscript. The citations are appropriate and accurately represent prior work.

result: Discussion claims provide evolutionary and developmental context, noting that reciprocal inhibition appears in limbed Amphibia while recurrent inhibition is mammalian-specific, V1 diversity is higher in mice than zebrafish, V1 synapses are affected early in ALS, Renshaw cells and Foxp2-V1s have distinct firing properties, and in vitro studies show sequential V1 generation from p1 progenitors can be influenced by retinoic acid signaling.
evaluation: Claims C93-C108 are discussion points supported by appropriate citations to prior literature. These contextualize the current findings within broader evolutionary, developmental, and disease contexts. The citations accurately represent prior work and the interpretations are reasonable.
